# HLF Pulse — Verified New Zealand Housing, Mortgage & KiwiSaver Reference Dataset

> Public reference dataset maintained by HLF (Home Loan Factory, https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/). Last verified: 10 November 2026 (2026-11-10T00:36:03Z).

## About the HLF Pulse
HLF Pulse is a public reference dataset covering New Zealand mortgage, housing and KiwiSaver statistics. Data is compiled from official releases from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Stats NZ, Inland Revenue and MBIE Tenancy Services.
Where HLF calculates percentages, averages or comparisons from the underlying official data, these are identified as 'Derived by HLF'. HLF does not alter or estimate official statistics. Where source data is unavailable, stale or cannot be verified, the relevant series is excluded until it can be confirmed.

## Machine-Readable Endpoints
- Structured Data Dictionary & Records (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/pulse.json
- Webflow Chat Bubble Feed (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-mortgage-pulse.json
- Main Reference Dataset Hub (HTML): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/

## Canonical Data Dictionary Pages
- [Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs investors (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/): Because mortgage applications often combine two incomes, approved first-home buyers in September 2026 recorded an average gross borrower income of $144.2k nationwide. [Calculation: Borrower-weighted mean across C41 TDTI bands = $144,232 (FHB)]
- [Annual residential construction cost inflation (CPI purchase of newly built home) (September 2026 quarter)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/build-cost-inflation/): Residential build-cost inflation has settled into single digits compared with the post-pandemic construction surge—Stats NZ recorded a +3.2% annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home in the September 2026 quarter, alongside 3.7% overall CPI inflation. [Calculation: Directly reported Stats NZ CPI purchase of new housing = +3.2% YoY]
- [First-home buyer high-DTI (>6x) lending share & bank speed-limit headroom (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/dti-headroom/): Most first-home lending currently sits well inside the Reserve Bank's Debt-to-Income limits—in September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer lending had a DTI ratio above 6x, sitting 10.9 percentage points below RBNZ's 20% bank speed-limit allowance. [Calculation: $139.0m ÷ $1,527.0m = 9.1% (Headroom: 20.0% - 9.1% = 10.9 pts)]
- [Total monthly dollar equity unlocked via mortgage top-ups (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/equity-topup-demand/): Tapping into home equity without selling is one of the most common moves in New Zealand banking—in September 2026, homeowners unlocked $962m in mortgage top-ups across 9,639 existing properties (averaging $100k per top-up). [Calculation: Directly reported $962m across 9,639 top-ups (Avg: $100k)]
- [First-home buyers approved with a 20% or greater deposit (<=80% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-20-deposit-club/): In September 2026, 1,325 first-home buyers (49.7% of first-home approvals, or $680m) were approved with a 20% or greater deposit (&le;80% LVR), borrowing an average of $513,208. In practice, a 20% deposit is the standard threshold where banks offer advertised special rates without low-equity margins. [Calculation: 1,325 ÷ 2,667 = 49.7% (Avg loan: $680m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208)]
- [Annual rolling 12-month first-home buyer mortgage approvals (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-annual-milestone/): Over the 12 months to September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 33,485 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $19.61B in lending (up from 31,589 loans a year earlier)—including 15,743 buyers (47.0%) who bought with under a 20% deposit. [Calculation: 12-month sum = 33,485 loans ($19,613m); <20% deposit share = 15,743 ÷ 33,485 = 47.0%]
- [First-home buyer share of all bank low-deposit (>80% LVR) lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-bank-lvr-priority/): First-home buyers account for the majority of bank low-deposit (&gt;80% LVR) mortgage approvals in New Zealand. In September 2026, 67.2% of all low-deposit mortgage dollars ($850m of $1.26B) and 62.0% of low-deposit loans (1,342 of 2,165) were committed to first-home buyers. [Calculation: Dollars: $850m ÷ $1,264m = 67.2% | Loans: 1,342 ÷ 2,165 = 62.0%]
- [Approved first-home buyer gross income — New Zealand vs Auckland (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-income-akl-vs-nz/): In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyers recorded a borrower-weighted average gross income of $144,232 nationwide in RBNZ Table C41. Because RBNZ combines single and joint mortgage applications, two-income households pull the headline average above single-earner norms. [Calculation: Harmonic mean across C41 bands = $144,232 (All NZ)]
- [First-home buyer average mortgage size by deposit tier (<20% vs 20%+ deposit) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-loan-size-gap/): In September 2026, New Zealand first-home buyers approved with under a 20% deposit (&gt;80% LVR) borrowed an average of $633,383, compared with $513,208 for buyers with a 20%+ deposit—a $120,175 difference. In practice, higher-income buyers often use low-deposit options to purchase sooner rather than waiting to accumulate a 20% deposit. [Calculation: ($850m ÷ 1,342 = $633,383) minus ($680m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208) = $120,175]
- [First-home buyers using under 20% deposit (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-low-deposit/): Buying a first home without a full 20% deposit is more common than many buyers expect. In September 2026, just over half of all first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (50.3%—1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) went to buyers with under a 20% deposit, up from 46.0% a year earlier. [Calculation: 1,342 ÷ 2,667 = 50.3% (Lending: $850m)]
- [Regional KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal averages across New Zealand (Year ended June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-regional-kiwisaver/): Over the year to June 2026, 50,330 first-home buyers withdrew $2.27B from KiwiSaver across New Zealand—averaging $45,005 per person nationwide (~$90,000 across two buyers), led by Wellington ($50,364/person) and Auckland ($47,630/person). [Calculation: $2,265,097,300 ÷ 50,330 members = $45,005/person (16 regions broken out below)]
- [First-home buyer share of total New Zealand mortgage lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-share/): First-home buyers continue to make up an active slice of the New Zealand market—in September 2026, banks approved 2,667 first-home mortgages (20.3% of all new mortgage lending, up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $574k. [Calculation: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Avg loan: $1,530m ÷ 2,667 = $574k)]
- [First-home buyers vs property investors monthly lending comparison (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-vs-investors/): First-home buyers are currently out-borrowing property investors in the Reserve Bank figures. In September 2026, banks approved $1.53B (20.3% of lending) for first-home buyers compared with $1.33B (17.7%) for property investors—putting first-home buyers $195m ahead. [Calculation: $1,530m (FHB) minus $1,335m (Investors) = +195m]
- [Interest-only share of new investor vs owner-occupier mortgages (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/interest-only/): Loan structures look quite different between rental properties and family homes in the Reserve Bank figures—in September 2026, 31.5% of new investor lending was set up on interest-only terms (including revolving credit), compared with 13.7% for owner-occupiers. [Calculation: Investors: $420m ÷ $1,335m = 31.5% | Owner-Occupiers: $828m ÷ $6,064m = 13.7%]
- [Property investor equity tier breakdown (40%+, 30%–40%, and <30% equity) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-equity-tiers/): Many property investors are buying with less than 40% equity. In September 2026, 43.8% of approved NZ property investors had 40%+ equity (&le;60% LVR)—while 36.4% bought in the 30%–40% equity band and 19.8% (527 loans, or $337m) were approved with under 30% equity. In practice, lender policy and LVR exemptions determine how much equity an individual investor needs. [Calculation: 40%+ eq: 1,169 ÷ 2,668 = 43.8% | 30–40% eq: 972 ÷ 2,668 = 36.4% | <30% eq: 527 ÷ 2,668 = 19.8%]
- [Property investor loans approved with under 20% deposit (>80% LVR) & 20%–30% deposit (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-low-deposit/): In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 52 investor mortgages ($36m, or 1.9% of investors) with strictly under a 20% deposit (&gt;80% LVR)—up from 34 loans ($23m) a year earlier (and 508 loans / $328m over the past 12 months)—plus another 475 investor loans ($301m, or 17.8%) in the 20%–30% deposit tier (70%–80% LVR). Under RBNZ rules, brand-new builds are exempt from LVR restrictions. [Calculation: >80% LVR: 52 ÷ 2,668 = 1.9% ($36m) | 70–80% LVR: 527 - 52 = 475 loans ($301m)]
- [Property investors approved with under a 30% deposit (>70% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-new-build-lvr/): Nearly one in five property investor mortgage approvals in New Zealand is written with less than a 30% deposit. In September 2026, 527 investor loans ($337m, or 19.8% of investor approvals) were approved with under a 30% deposit (&gt;70% LVR)—comprising 475 loans ($301m) in the 20%–30% deposit band and 52 loans ($36m) with under a 20% deposit (&gt;80% LVR). Under RBNZ rules, new builds are exempt from LVR restrictions alongside bank speed limits. [Calculation: 527 ÷ 2,668 = 19.8% (475 loans in 70–80% LVR + 52 loans in >80% LVR)]
- [Investor vs owner-occupier interest-only mortgage share (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-vs-owner-io/): Loan structures look quite different between rental properties and family homes in the Reserve Bank figures—in September 2026, 31.5% of new investor lending was set up on interest-only terms (including revolving credit), compared with 13.7% for owner-occupiers. [Calculation: Investors: $420m ÷ $1,335m = 31.5% | Owner-Occupiers: $828m ÷ $6,064m = 13.7%]
- [Property investor share of new New Zealand mortgage lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investors/): First-home buyers are currently borrowing more overall than property investors—in September 2026, investors made up 17.7% of new mortgage lending ($1.33B, down from 21.2% a year earlier), compared with 20.3% for first-home buyers. [Calculation: $1,335m ÷ $7,533m = 17.7%]
- [Active KiwiSaver provider switching volume (Year ended June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kiwisaver-active-switchers/): Reviewing and changing KiwiSaver providers happens more regularly than many members realise—over the year to June 2026, 198,897 New Zealanders moved their balance to a new scheme, averaging 16,575 switches every month. [Calculation: 198,897 annual transfers ÷ 12 months = 16,575/month]
- [Monthly KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal count, value & average per buyer (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kiwisaver-first-home/): For many buyers, KiwiSaver does much of the heavy lifting toward a first deposit—in September 2026, 4,250 members withdrew a combined $195.7m to put toward a first home—averaging ~$46k per withdrawing member, or roughly $73k of KiwiSaver funds per approved first-home mortgage. [Calculation: $195.7m ÷ 4,250 members = ~$46k/member | $195.7m ÷ 2,667 FHB loans = ~$73k/loan]
- [Annual and monthly KiwiSaver scheme transfers (members switching providers) (Year ended June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kiwisaver-switches/): Reviewing and changing KiwiSaver providers happens more regularly than many members realise—over the year to June 2026, 198,897 New Zealanders moved their balance to a new scheme, averaging 16,575 switches every month. [Calculation: 198,897 annual transfers ÷ 12 months = 16,575/month]
- [Existing owner-occupiers approved with under 20% equity (>80% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/mover-low-equity/): Low-deposit lending is not restricted to first-home buyers. In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 769 mortgages ($378m) for existing owner-occupiers moving or borrowing with under 20% equity (&gt;80% LVR)—accounting for 5.1% of existing homeowner approvals, up from 3.3% a year earlier. [Calculation: 769 ÷ 15,096 = 5.1%]
- [Annual new residential dwellings consented in New Zealand (Year ended September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/new-builds-annual/): New-build supply across New Zealand has been gathering pace, with 41,091 new homes consented in the year to September 2026 (up 18.0% on the previous year, including 3,570 dwellings consented in September 2026). [Calculation: Directly reported Stats NZ annual total = 41,091 (3,570 in September 2026)]
- [Existing owner-occupiers approved with 20% or more equity (<=80% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/owner-equity-buffer/): The vast majority of existing owner-occupier mortgage approvals involve borrowers with at least 20% equity. In September 2026, 94.9% of existing owner-occupier mortgages approved across New Zealand (14,327 of 15,096 loans, or $4.16B) had 20% or more equity (&le;80% LVR), carrying an average loan size of $290,082. [Calculation: 14,327 ÷ 15,096 = 94.9% (Avg loan: $4,156m ÷ 14,327 = $290,082)]
- [Monthly mortgage refinancing (borrowers switching bank providers) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/refinance/): Moving banks is a regular part of the New Zealand mortgage market rather than a rare step—in September 2026 alone, 2,772 borrowers switched mortgage providers, moving $1.73B in loans (23.0% of all new lending, at an average loan size of $624k). [Calculation: $1,729m ÷ $7,533m = 23.0% (Avg loan: $1,729m ÷ 2,772 = $624k)]
- [New Zealand national and regional median weekly private rent (August 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/rent-yield-pulse/): Private weekly rents across New Zealand have been relatively steady over the past year—the national median sat at $595/wk in August 2026 (up 0.8% on a year earlier), with regional medians at $650/wk in Auckland, $580/wk in Wellington, and $550/wk in Canterbury. [Calculation: Reported national median = $595/wk; YoY = ($595 - $590) ÷ $590 = +0.8%]
- [Monthly newly lodged and active private rental bonds in New Zealand (August 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/rental-bonds-supply/): Thousands of New Zealand households sign new leases every month—Tenancy Services logged 13,062 newly lodged private rental bonds in August 2026, across a nationwide pool of 522,942 active private tenancies. [Calculation: Directly reported MBIE 'ALL' location: 13,062 lodged bonds & 522,942 active bonds]
- [Weighted-average settled 1-year and 2-year fixed mortgage interest rates (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/settled-rates/): Across all new fixed residential mortgages settled in September 2026, New Zealand borrowers locked in a weighted-average interest rate of 4.82% for one year and 5.09% for two years in RBNZ Table B30. [Calculation: Directly reported RBNZ B30 series NCFA.MAM1PR.D1 = 4.82% (1Y) & NCFA.MAM1PR.D2 = 5.09% (2Y)]
- [New Zealand median student loan balance (June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/student-loan-servicing/): Student debt is a familiar line item on home loan applications—across Inland Revenue's June 2026 figures, the median NZ student loan balance sat at $18,301 (up 4.5% on a year earlier), where compulsory PAYE deductions factor into how banks test monthly servicing. [Calculation: Directly reported IRD median = $18,301 (Change: ($18,301 - $17,516) ÷ $17,516 = +4.5%)]
- [Monthly mortgage top-ups on existing properties (borrower share & average top-up) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/top-ups/): Many Kiwi homeowners tap into existing equity for renovations or upgrades rather than moving house—in September 2026, 9,639 borrowers topped up an existing mortgage, making up 46.4% of all mortgage approvals by count (average top-up: $100k). [Calculation: 9,639 ÷ 20,763 = 46.4% (Avg top-up: $962m ÷ 9,639 = $100k)]
- [Multi-unit and townhouse share of new residential building consents (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/townhouse-share/): Townhouses and multi-unit developments now make up more than half of new residential consents—accounting for 51.5% (1,837 of 3,570 homes) consented in September 2026, including 1,305 townhouses, flats, and units. [Calculation: (3,570 total minus 1,733 stand-alone houses) = 1,837 ÷ 3,570 = 51.5%]
